blocks.text: This article provides the requirements to use a Browser Access application with a certificate.
When using a certificate, the following prerequisites apply:

blocks.item: Your FQDN for the application must be properly named (e.g., web.example1.com), and your App Connectors must resolve to that hostname via your internal DNS. The tenant must own the domain.
Web servers must serve pages with objects linked as relative URLs (e.g., HREF=”/filename.ext”).
If an application uses the HTTP header Content-Security-Policy, then the application must accept an external FQDN in the host/origin header.
You must upload a combined PEM file containing the following:

blocks.text: After you define an application segment with Browser Access enabled, you must create a browser token validator.
When using a certificate, the following items aren't supported:

blocks.item: Browser Access applications must be modified to add absolute external URLs.
Wildcard cookies and wildcard Browser Access applications (e.g., *.example1.com)
Unregistered domains in your account (e.g., testing.com)

Applications sending Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) requests to Browser Access applications (e.g., the application web.example1.com sends a CORS request to the Browser Access application images.example1.com)
